reflection_mode.description: Standing self-reflection. When enabled, a session distills SANITIZED, generalized workflow-improvement candidates into the backlog sub-workflow at session end (after the kickoff prompt) AND authors ONLY to the backlog — it never edits the living doc. Default ON, natural-language-toggleable. State-tracked rather than an ad-hoc prose token (state-over-tokens).

operator_autonomy.description: A STANDING operator grant that changes what a position class DOES, recorded here rather than re-conveyed in kickoff prose (state-over-tokens). The kickoff is convenience and explicitly non-authoritative, so a grant carried only there is invisible to a session that starts from state alone — which then defaults back to WAIT and contradicts the standing intent. Additive and fully optional, so plans authored before this stay valid. IT FAILS SAFE BY ABSENCE: an absent object, or an absent/false flag, means the position class behaves as written and WAITS; a grant is never inferred from a session's tone, from work proceeding smoothly, or from a prior session having proceeded. Rule-bearing, so it is REPLACED IN PLACE when the operator's standing intent changes, never appended to.

proceed_past_phase_boundaries.description: When true, a phase_boundary opener presents the register as it already owes and then proceeds autonomously with per-decision logging, instead of waiting. NARROW by construction: it reaches phase_boundary only — a hitl_opening still waits, and every human-gated item still gates — because the grant's whole warrant is that the operator reads the committed end-state.

provenance.description: The operator authorization this grant rests on, carried here exactly as a sanctioned OVERRIDE carries its own in the decisions register. An unrecorded go-ahead is a defect; a grant with no provenance cannot be told from one a session invented for itself.

conditions.description: What the grant obliges in exchange — canonically that every decision taken past the boundary is documented — plus any scope the operator attached to it.

ecosystem.description: Every environmental property resolved at COLD START and read thereafter — capabilities, host execution constraints, and the named per-repo properties (commit_ownership, integration_posture) — not capabilities alone. Never assume host/runtime/tools; encode divergences as 'if capability absent -> do Y'. Capability names are ecosystem-agnostic; values are the resolved primitive for this ecosystem.

integration_posture.description: The host's standing ROUTE from a local change to a landed one, resolved at cold start from host properties (never branched on a host name) as a THIRD per-repo property beside commit_ownership and the co-occupancy condition. Typed rather than left to the freeform capabilities map because it is a per-repo PROPERTY like commit_ownership, not a capability binding, and because downstream rules dereference it: with no fixed shape, two sessions resolving the same host record non-comparable answers. TWO LEVELS, deliberately not the same: no field is schema-REQUIRED, so plans authored before this stay valid and backfill when they re-pin; but a session that actually RESOLVES a posture is expected to record all four, including where an answer is the permissive default, because a reader cannot distinguish an unresolved posture from a resolved permissive one. Validation stays lenient so the obligation is the protocol's, not the harness's.

default_vehicle.description: Whether ordinary work commits directly on a branch in the shared checkout or always goes through the isolation-plus-integration vehicle; carries the concrete vehicle bound at resolve time and the location that satisfies the dev-environment activation/trust-scope property.

draft_policy.description: Whether the host's integration request has a draft state and whether draft SUPPRESSES automated review, plus the resolved intent split — a progress surface stays draft, work handed over for review is opened ready wherever draft would gate it.

phase_branch_review_binding.description: How phase, branch and review unit bind on this host. Recorded like every sibling once a posture is resolved — including where the answer is the default phase = branch = review sitting, per the record-all-four expectation above — since an omitted field is indistinguishable from an unresolved one. The case that motivated typing it is a host whose review unit spans several phases.

push_point.description: When work is pushed, warranted by durability and cross-session visibility rather than by concurrency.

execution_mode.description: Operating mode resolved at cold start, a confirmed input not an inference: 'web-run' (no-repo/document-only — everything in the single regenerated plan doc; leak-safety relaxed) or 'cli' (repo-backed, single machine — working state out-of-repo under <xdg-state-base>/<clone-name>/<workflow-name>/, durable knowledge committed).

execution_mode_history.description: Ordered ledger of the mode segments this plan has run in — a plan may cross the web<->cli boundary more than once, so this ledger, not the single current execution_mode, is the complete provenance of where the plan has been. Appended at cold start and at each transition.

capabilities.description: map of capability-name -> resolved primitive; an ABSENT resolution records the probe that produced it alongside its fallback — a negative result is falsifiable, a present resolution self-proving on use.

execution_constraints.description: Host execution/resource constraints resolved at cold start: resource ceilings, sandbox/rate limits, each with its safe workaround recipe. Read every session, never re-derived.

living_doc_baseline.description: VERSION pin for the canonical living doc + shared harness this plan was authored against (DRY-by-reference). Dependents read the living doc at this version. 'path' identifies the master living doc; under XDG a running plan resolves it to the INSTALLED skill's references/ copy (bundled with the harness + changelog as same-dir siblings), while version->commit reconciliation resolves against the nix-agentic-tools source checkout. 'version' is the assigned identity the doc carries as content (a monotonic ordinal + a distinctive label), NOT a raw commit hash — it resolves to a commit by derive-from-history (the commit that assigned it) and also travels to a document-only artifact that has no commit. In a resident-commits repo the resident stamps the shipped version at commit time; until then 'version' holds the sentinel 'PENDING-RESIDENT-STAMP'. State-tracked rather than an ad-hoc prose token (state-over-tokens).

parent.description: Nesting pointer for a child of a downstream PROJECT plan: records the parent plan and the return pointer, so on the child's TERMINAL FOLD the kickoff chain RETURNS to its PARENT. For project work only — not the backlog's own inline fold. Absent on any top-level plan (a project root or the backlog sub-workflow).

done_condition.description: What must be TRUE for this phase to be FINISHED — its exit criterion, distinct from the runnable-increment constraint (which says only what a phase must PRODUCE). Required by the master's GREEDY SCHEDULER when a phase is written; additive/optional here so plans authored before it stay schema-valid, and backfilled when a dependent re-pins. With this slot empty the open-items register drifts into the completion criterion by default and 'done' becomes 'the register is empty' — unsatisfiable by construction, since the register grows with discovery and discovery scales with carefulness. Write it to stay satisfiable: a clause that verifies against an upstream source the work itself absorbs or deletes becomes unsatisfiable exactly by succeeding.

disposition.description: HITL@Pn | DEFAULT:<x>(revisable) | AI-OWNED | RESOLVED | BACKLOG | GROOMED | NEEDS-EVIDENCE:<what-would-decide-it> | FOLDED | DROPPED:<reason>. NEEDS-EVIDENCE parks an item that is plausible but not yet decidable: it names the evidence that would settle it and waits for that evidence to accrue, rather than being decided on a single sighting or discarded. It is a HOLD, not a terminal state.

pinned.description: Optional flag marking an open_item as pinned in the live register so it is not drained — e.g. a parked NEEDS-EVIDENCE candidate that accrues sightings across passes rather than being re-decided or removed.

entry.description: relative path to the backlog entry file, when this open_item is a rolling-backlog candidate

park_clock.description: Expiry clock for a parked NEEDS-EVIDENCE entry (backlog grooming park lifecycle). 'anchor' = date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last new sighting or an operator clock-reset, whichever is later; the park's expiry window is a backlog-rules constant (currently 90 days, wall-clock) measured from it. A new sighting or an operator reset updates the anchor. Only meaningful while disposition is NEEDS-EVIDENCE; additive/optional — plans that never park carry no clock.
